# Long debt cycle

Short business cycles ride on top of a much longer one. Over decades, debt grows faster than income, because each recession is met with easier credit and each recovery starts from a higher level of borrowing.

The long debt cycle is the multi-decade rise and fall of total debt relative to income. ^debt-def

## Upswing

Borrowing lifts spending, spending lifts incomes and asset prices, and higher asset prices support more borrowing. The loop is self-reinforcing and feels like prosperity. Lenders relax standards because recent defaults have been low.

## Top

The cycle turns when debt service grows faster than the income available to pay it and interest rates cannot fall further. See [[Minsky moment]].

## Downswing

What follows is [[Deleveraging]]: years in which debt is paid down, written off or inflated away.
